key_insight: Learn the dissipation potential—not the constitutive law directly—to guarantee convexity, frame-indifference, and dissipativity, making the inverse problem well-posed by design.
engineering_relevance: This provides a safer way to infer material behavior from indirect velocity data in fluid and solid-like continua, with better stability and transfer to unseen geometries.
method: Use an input-convex neural network (ICNNE) to parameterize the dissipation potential.
Enforce frame-indifference and evenness in the second strain-rate invariant by symmetrization.
Penalize nonzero gradient at the origin and couple Firedrake + PyTorch for PDE-constrained training.
evidence_signal: The method is tested on four benchmarks—compressible Navier-Stokes, Herschel-Bulkley flow, Hibler sea-ice, and DEM data—and reports recovery of known physics, accurate transfer to unseen geometries, and success where unstructured methods diverge.
watch_item: The approach relies on weak penalty enforcement for dissipativity and on coupled PDE/NN training, so optimization and implementation details may affect robustness and cost.
paper_title: Well-posed by Design: Learning Constitutive Laws from Velocity Data using Convex Neural Network Potentials
